name: יָרִיב
summary: Borne by one of the heads whom Ezra sent for at the river Ahava to bring Levites for the house of God (Ezr 8:16), by a priest of the sons of Jeshua son of Jozadak who had married a foreign wife (Ezr 10:18), and, in Chronicles' list, by a son of Simeon called Jachin in Genesis, Exodus and Numbers (1Ch 4:24; Gen 46:10). The name is the qal imperfect of רִיב, “he contends” or “he pleads the cause”, the very form scripture uses of Yahweh pleading his people's cause (Pro 23:11; Jer 50:34; Mic 7:9); the same word is the noun יָרִיב “opponent” (Psa 35:1).

evidence.note: “I sent for Eliezer … and for Jarib (וּלְיָרִיב) … heads.”
Among the priests with foreign wives: “Maaseiah, Eliezer, וְיָרִיב and Gedaliah.”
“The sons of Simeon: Nemuel and Jamin, Jarib, Zerah, Shaul.”
The same son of Simeon named יָכִין, Jachin (also Exo 6:15; Num 26:12).
“Their redeemer is strong; he will plead (הוּא־יָרִיב) their cause against you”: the form of the name.

note: Takes t.cm.af; its count includes ten qal יָרִיב verb tokens filed by spelling (Jdg 6:31; Isa 50:8 etc.), so the name's real uses are Ezr 8:16; 10:18; 1Ch 4:24. TIPNR keys the Simeonite as Jachin@Gen.46.10 with Jarib as a form; tagged here as he bears this name in 1Ch 4:24. Whether Jarib and Jachin are two names of one man or a copyist's change in one letter is not settled; a Jachin name file (root כון) would also tag him. The reading “he contends” takes the name as a bare verb with no subject; a divine subject is implied by the fuller name Joiarib, “Yahweh contends”.
